posts.author: a_k
posts.content_md:
Hello everyone,

I have been thinking about starting a pdf collection about holography similar to the Lippmann collection but in a more structured form. Submissions could be as simple as sending me an email or having a dedicated section where the pdfs can be uploaded as attachments to a posting. The pdf format is preferred but texts in other formats are also welcome and would be converted to pdf here.

The critical point is the copyright issue. There are many texts in the public domain. For others the authors would need to be contacted to get their permission to include them in the collection. I can offer this service at least for the start, maybe others could participate.

What do you think, interested? Any texts you could contribute or any suggestions?

posts.author: dannybee
posts.content_md: maybe a pdf of where to get reasonable supplies and lasers, I think it would be a olive branch of a idea

posts.author: Steven
posts.content_md:
That would be very useful Ahmet.

Would the documents be added to the reading room/wiki?

Steven.

posts.author: a_k
posts.content_md:
The structured pdf collection would be accessed the same way as the Lippmann collection, through the archives section. 

Come on Danny, please (this is no request anymore - i won't tell you a 4th time) try to stick to the topic. Your beloved one is on ebay, the same name as here.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
Ahmet, I sent a test pdf file (a 1969 paper by Brandes et al. on DCG) to your admin. address (we were having spam-filtering problems when sending to hispeed).

I have a pdf file generator in my business software, but it prints an annoying advertisement on the bottom of each page, which can't be removed. I can send pretty large documents (maybe 15 pages at 400dpi scan) and the files are fairly small and quick to email. It has some kind of function in the software which minimizes the file size, yet still provides a good copy.

On the file I sent, Corel Draw was used to generate the 3-page .pdf file, scanned at only 175dpi, yet the file size was around 4MB.

It's mainly a question of how quickly and efficiently I can scan the pages and get them to you, in a usable format. The pages I recently posted on the forum were simply scanned in jpg and inserted into the post. It's fairly fast that way, but it's not pdf. My scanner has a pdf function, but haven't tried it. My computer skills are quite limited. When time allows, I will look for better ways of scanning/sending, hopefully in pdf.

This is the jpg paper:

posts.author: a_k
posts.content_md:
Thanks Joe, received the document. It can be accessed in the archive section -> holoforum pdf collection

For the moment i'll move icoming documents directly into the flat directory, the structure will be organised a bit later. I would be grateful for all suggestions about a sensible hierarchy structure.

There is no rush joe, you can also send any format, i can batch convert them to pdf without much effort, just have to prepare scripts/lookup the syntax of existing scripts.

Hi Joe,

I just converted the first jpg of the document you just posted to a PDF, using IrfanView.

The resulting file size came out at 530k, which is smaller than the original jpg.

I used the default setting in IrfanView and disabled password security in the PDF check box.

IrfanView is free for none commercial use and can be downloaded here:

[http://www.irfanview.com/](http://www.irfanview.com/)

There is also a wiki page on the software:

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IrfanView](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IrfanView)

Oh, and there is no annoying advertisement on the the page. 

HTH,

Steven.
